section_summary: This section contains the Rules of the House of Councillors, covering its officers, committees, proceedings, petitions, relations with other bodies, and discipline. An accompanying title page introduces the Law for the Election of Members of the House of Councillors. The portion of that law shown sets out constituencies, eligibility, voting and counting procedures, and rules for candidates and elected members.

subfiles.title: Rules of the House of Councillors
subfiles.about: Rules governing the organization and proceedings of Japan's House of Councillors.
subfiles.summary: The rules prescribe how the House elects officers, nominates a prime minister, handles bills, and conducts committee work and plenary meetings. They also regulate voting, interpellations, minutes, petitions, relations with the House of Representatives and government offices, visitors, member conduct, and disciplinary proceedings.

subfiles.title: Accompaniment to Despatch No. 160: Law for the Election of Members of the House of Councillors
subfiles.from: Government Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Title page identifying the election law as an accompaniment to a despatch from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the accompanying election law as passed by the 92nd Diet.

subfiles.title: Law for the Election of Members of the House of Councillors
subfiles.about: Statutory provisions for electing members from prefectural and national constituencies.
subfiles.summary: The law allocates 250 House seats between prefectural and national constituencies and defines voting rights, eligibility, election oversight, and election timing. It specifies ballot casting and counting, election meetings, candidacy and deposits, and how winners are determined. The portion shown also addresses declined or invalid elections and circumstances requiring a new election; the text continues beyond page 415.
